basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 1.' and it opens '(Cap. XLVIII.—Vers. 1.) Et nuntiatum est Joseph, Ecce pater tuus aegrotat: et tulit duos'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XLVIII.—Vers. 1.) Et nuntiatum est Joseph, Ecce pater tuus aegrotat: et tulit duos filios secum, Manassen et Ephraim. Et ex hoc illud quod supra diximus, demonstratur, quia Joseph ad id locorum duos tantum filios habuerit, Ephraim et Manassen. Si enim post multos annos, moriente Jacob patre suo, duos tantummodo filios duxit ad benedictionem, utique illo tempore, cum filii ejus generare non quiverant, parvuli atque lactentes, in ingressu patris et fratrum, nepotes ex eis habere non potuit.
